title: Ordinary isomorphism-square mate on completed-module sections
statement: For an adic coefficient datum d and a chosen Cartesian scheme square (v,p prime,p,g) with v and g scheme isomorphisms, the specified purReindexingModuleMate is invertible. On M and a test V over Y, its value after the inverse-image unit for g is restriction of the inverse-image unit for v along the canonical fibre-product pasting isomorphism purReindexingTestSquare(sq.w). This statement concerns the ordinary module mate only and asserts no tower or derived exchange result. The coefficient datum and the concrete canonical maps are those of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and [def-pur-completed-reindexing-data].

proof.text: For each test over Y prime restrict sections along (v,1) between the two fibre products. Its inverse is (inv v,1), because commutativity and cancellation of g give the required equality over Y prime. Coefficient composition gives module linearity, and fibre-product functoriality gives naturality in tests and modules.

Use the comma-normalized section reindexing of lem-pur-completed-module-section-reindexing. The transpose of this restriction map is the canonical pullback-square identification followed by the pulled counit: both restrict a local section along (v,W to V). The tensor-unit normalization and sheafification extend the local equation. Uniqueness of adjunction transpose therefore identifies it with purReindexingModuleMate and yields exactly its stated unit-normalized section formula.
